name: Milwaukee
title: Investor Renovation Contractor in Milwaukee, WI | Genstone
metaDescription: Milwaukee investor rehabs for flips, BRRRR, rentals, duplexes, 203(k) and REO. Scopes built around Polish flats, cream city brick and lead-era systems.
intro: Milwaukee rewards investors who understand what is behind the plaster. The city is full of upper-and-lower duplexes, Polish flats, worker cottages and brick bungalows that cash-flow well, but nearly all of them were built before 1978, many still carry original galvanized water lines, and a good share sit on stone or block foundations that have spent a century soaking up Lake Michigan weather. Genstone Construction plans and manages renovations for investors, lenders and servicers buying in Milwaukee, coordinating vetted, licensed local contractors while our estimators and field managers run the job from our Romeoville, Illinois headquarters. Every project starts with a free Pre-Offer Rehab Review so you see repair costs and a refined after-repair value before you commit capital, then moves to a written scope with a draw schedule and a field manager who stays with the property from demolition to final billing. You pay nothing upfront, draws follow completed work, and dumpster costs are already in the estimate.
housingStock:
Most of Milwaukee's investor inventory was built between the 1880s and the 1950s, and the era tells you a lot about the scope before you walk in.

The oldest layer sits close to the core: Walker's Point, Brewers Hill, Riverwest and the near south side hold balloon-framed worker cottages and narrow two-story frame houses, some faced in the pale cream city brick the city is known for. Balloon framing matters on a rehab because the wall cavities run uninterrupted from basement to attic, so fire blocking has to be added when walls are opened, and old knob-and-tube circuits often survive in those cavities long after the panel was replaced.

The south side, from Lincoln Village through Bay View and Jackson Park, is the home of the Polish flat: a cottage that was jacked up so a second, partly below-grade unit could be built beneath it. Those lower units tend to have low ceilings, small windows and moisture issues, and they decide whether the property works as a duplex or should be returned to single-family use.

On the north and west sides, Sherman Park, Washington Heights and Harambee are dense with upper-and-lower duplexes and Arts and Crafts bungalows from the 1910s through the 1920s, usually with separate entries, separate meters on the better-updated buildings, and shared basements. Farther west and south, Enderis Park, Story Hill and Layton Park move into brick Tudors, bungalows and post-war Cape Cods and ranches with poured or block foundations.

For a rehab budget that means three recurring line items: lead-safe practices on nearly every job, plumbing replacement where galvanized supply and cast-iron drains remain, and basement water management on foundations that were never designed to stay dry.

commonIssues.title: Lead hazards in paint and water service
commonIssues.body: Nearly the entire Milwaukee rental stock predates the 1978 lead paint ban, and the city has long treated childhood lead exposure as a priority. Window sashes, porches and trim are the usual hazard points. Separately, many older homes are still fed by a lead water service line from the street. Budget for lead-safe work practices by certified renovators, plan window replacement or treatment early, and confirm the service line material before you finalize a rental or resale plan.

commonIssues.title: Stone and block foundations
commonIssues.body: Fieldstone and rubble foundations under pre-1920 houses let water and soil in through failed mortar joints, and many have been parged over several times. Block foundations from the 1940s and 1950s tend to bow inward from frost and saturated clay. A good scope separates cosmetic efflorescence from active movement, prices tuckpointing or bracing honestly, and adds drain tile and a sump where the basement takes water every spring.

commonIssues.title: Galvanized supply and cast-iron drains
commonIssues.body: Older Milwaukee duplexes often keep their original galvanized supply lines, which narrow with scale until upper units lose pressure, and cast-iron stacks that crack along the seams. Replacing supply piping with PEX or copper and opening stacks where they run through finished walls is common. Scoping the main drain with a camera before closing is worth doing on anything with mature trees nearby, since clay laterals and root intrusion show up regularly.

commonIssues.title: Knob-and-tube and undersized service
commonIssues.body: Balloon-framed houses and early duplexes frequently hide knob-and-tube wiring in walls even when the basement shows modern cable. Many two-unit buildings also run both apartments from undersized services. Insurers and lenders often push back on any remaining knob-and-tube, so the electrical line item usually grows once walls are open. A Pre-Offer Rehab Review flags the likely scope so it is in your offer, not in a change order.

commonIssues.title: Porches, chimneys and masonry
commonIssues.body: Two-story front porches on duplexes take a beating from freeze-thaw and often need structural work, new decking and code-compliant guards. Brick chimneys lose mortar and crowns, and soft cream city brick cannot be repointed with hard modern mortar without damaging it. Expect porch and masonry work to show up on a large share of older properties, and price it as its own phase so it can be scheduled for warmer months.

investorMarket:
Milwaukee works for several strategies at once, but they cluster in different parts of town.

Buy-and-hold investors focus on the north side and near west side, where duplexes and single-family houses in neighborhoods like Sherman Park, Washington Park and Amani can be bought at prices that support rental cash flow. The rehab there is usually about systems, safety and durability rather than design, and the tenant base relies heavily on steady, well-maintained housing.

Flippers tend to work where owner-occupant buyers are competing: Bay View, Tosa-adjacent pockets on the west side such as Washington Heights and Enderis Park, and parts of Riverwest. Buyers in those areas notice original woodwork, finished hardwoods and updated kitchens, so a flip there needs real finish decisions and clean inspection results.

BRRRR investors often land between those two zones, in south side neighborhoods like Jackson Park and Layton Park or the far northwest, where an all-in rehab can still appraise well because comparable homes have been updated.

Small multifamily is the city's signature asset. Upper-and-lower duplexes appear in almost every older neighborhood, which gives investors a deep pool to buy from and an appraiser pool used to valuing them.

Finally, the city and lenders have handled a steady flow of tax-foreclosed and bank-owned houses for years, so REO and distressed acquisitions remain a meaningful part of the market.
permits:
Building permits inside city limits are issued by the City of Milwaukee Department of Neighborhood Services, which also handles code enforcement and inspections. Structural work, new or relocated walls, porch rebuilds, roofing, and most electrical, plumbing and HVAC work require a permit, and trade permits are pulled by licensed contractors. Wisconsin licenses electricians, plumbers and HVAC installers at the state level through the Department of Safety and Professional Services, and one- and two-family dwellings fall under the state's Uniform Dwelling Code.

Two local items deserve attention on investor jobs. First, the Department of Neighborhood Services runs a vacant building registration program, so owners and servicers holding empty houses need to be registered and keep the property secured and maintained. Second, open code orders follow the property, and a house bought from a servicer or at tax sale may come with outstanding violations that have to be cleared through inspection.

Suburbs such as Wauwatosa, West Allis and Shorewood each run their own building departments, with their own inspectors and permit processes. Genstone tracks which jurisdiction a property sits in and builds permit and inspection steps into the schedule.
climate:
Milwaukee's weather shapes rehab work as much as the housing age does. Winters are long and cold, with lake-effect moisture near the shoreline, so ice dams on poorly insulated attics are common, and frost reaches deep enough to heave porches and push on foundation walls. Spring brings the most basement water as snowmelt and rain saturate clay soils, which is the right time to see how a basement really behaves.

On scheduling, exterior work such as roofing, masonry, tuckpointing, porch rebuilds and concrete is best done between late spring and fall. Interior work carries on through winter, but vacant houses need heat maintained throughout, and a house that froze during a vacancy often hides burst supply lines and cracked boilers. Plan winter acquisitions with a full plumbing and heating test before scoping finishes.

faqs.q: Does Genstone have an office in Milwaukee?
faqs.a: No. Genstone Construction is headquartered in Romeoville, Illinois, and our estimators, field managers and billing team run Milwaukee projects from there. On the ground, we coordinate vetted, licensed and insured local contractors in the Milwaukee market. Your designated field manager oversees the work, manages inspections and posts progress and documentation so you can follow the project without driving to the property.

faqs.q: Should I keep a Polish flat as a duplex or convert it?
faqs.a: It depends on the lower unit. If it has workable ceiling height, legal egress windows, a dry floor and its own heat, keeping two units usually supports rental income and appraisal. If the lower level is damp, low and dark, the cost of making it a decent apartment may exceed what it adds. Our Pre-Offer Rehab Review can price both paths so you compare them before you buy.

faqs.q: How do you handle lead paint on Milwaukee rehabs?
faqs.a: We plan it into the scope from the start. Work that disturbs painted surfaces in pre-1978 housing is done with lead-safe practices by certified renovators, and windows, porches and friction surfaces are addressed as part of the plan rather than as an afterthought. That approach keeps rental and resale plans on track and avoids surprise work after a tenant or buyer is in place.

faqs.q: Can you work on properties outside the city of Milwaukee?
faqs.a: Yes. We work across Milwaukee County and nearby communities such as Wauwatosa, West Allis, Cudahy, Greenfield and Glendale. Each suburb has its own building department and inspection process, so our scope and schedule are built around the jurisdiction the property actually sits in. Housing in those suburbs also differs from the city: West Allis and Cudahy have many small post-war bungalows and ranches, while Wauwatosa and Shorewood lean toward larger pre-war homes where buyers expect a higher finish level.

fix-flip.title: Fix and Flip Contractor in Milwaukee, WI | Genstone
fix-flip.metaDescription: Fix and flip renovations in Milwaukee built for buyers in Bay View, Washington Heights and Riverwest. Free pre-offer rehab review and draws tied to work.
fix-flip.h1: Fix and Flip Renovations in Milwaukee
fix-flip.intro: A Milwaukee flip lives or dies on two things buyers check closely: whether the old house has been properly modernized behind the walls, and whether the finishes match what has already sold on the block. Owner-occupant buyers in Bay View, Washington Heights and Riverwest are paying for character, so stripping out every piece of oak trim can hurt you as much as leaving a 1960s kitchen. Genstone Construction scopes Milwaukee flips with your exit in mind. Our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review prices the repairs, tests your after-repair value against what those buyers have paid, and tells you whether the deal supports your offer. From there you get a detailed scope with finish options, a field manager who runs the job, and draws released only as work is completed.

sections.h2: Match the finish level to the Milwaukee block
sections.body: The same budget behaves very differently depending on where the house sits. In Bay View, buyers expect refinished hardwood, an updated but not sterile kitchen, and a bathroom that respects the age of the house; painted original millwork tends to sell better than a full gut. In Washington Heights and Story Hill, the comparison set is often brick bungalows and Tudors with built-ins and leaded glass, so preserving those features while replacing systems is usually where the value lies. On the far south side, ranch and Cape Cod buyers are more focused on a clean basement, newer mechanicals and an open kitchen. Our estimators build more than one finish plan when the comps support it, so you can see what moving from a rental-grade finish to a buyer-grade finish costs and what it is likely to add. That choice is made before you buy, not halfway through demolition. It also keeps you from overbuilding a house on a block where the top sale was a modest rental-grade rehab, which is a common way Milwaukee flips lose money.

sections.h2: Pass the buyer's inspection on an old Milwaukee house
sections.body: Buyers of century-old Milwaukee homes almost always hire an inspector, and the report tends to focus on the same items: remaining knob-and-tube, galvanized supply lines, a wet or bowing basement wall, an aging boiler or furnace, and loose porch railings. A flip that dresses up the kitchen but leaves those conditions in place often gives the profit back in negotiation. We put those systems first in the scope. Electrical updates and plumbing replacement are done under permit with the Department of Neighborhood Services, foundation and drainage repairs are documented, and lead-safe practices are followed on painted surfaces. When the listing goes live, you can hand buyers a clean story: what was replaced, when, and by whom, with permits closed and photos from your field manager's progress log. Lead-safe documentation matters to many buyers with young children, and a camera scope of the sewer lateral is cheap insurance on a lot with old street trees. Where a basement wall has been braced or drain tile added, the paperwork helps the buyer's lender and inspector understand that the issue was corrected rather than hidden behind fresh paint.

sections.h2: Control carrying costs through a Wisconsin winter
sections.body: Holding costs climb quickly when a flip stalls, and Milwaukee weather is the most common reason projects stall. Roofing, masonry repair on soft cream city brick, porch rebuilds and exterior paint all need workable temperatures, so a house bought in late fall should have its exterior work priced and either finished quickly or deliberately deferred to spring. Interior trades can keep moving through winter if heat is maintained, which is why we test heating and plumbing first on every winter acquisition. Your draw schedule is written around these realities, with exterior phases separated from interior ones so a cold snap delays one line rather than the whole job. Spring is typically when buyer activity picks up, so many investors plan to have the house finished and staged before the market turns. Your field manager reports progress against each milestone without you needing to be on site, so if a supplier delay or an unexpected stack replacement threatens the listing date, you hear about it early enough to adjust. Genstone Financial also offers fix-and-flip loans and lines of credit for investors who want purchase and rehab funding from the same group.

faqs.q: How fast can a Milwaukee flip get started?
faqs.a: Once you accept the scope and estimate, your field manager lines up licensed local contractors and pulls the permits the work requires through the Department of Neighborhood Services. Demolition and work that does not need a permit can often begin first. Start dates depend on the scope and the season, and we will tell you plainly where the schedule depends on permits or weather.

faqs.q: Will you keep original woodwork and hardwood floors?
faqs.a: When it helps the sale, yes. In many Milwaukee neighborhoods, refinished original floors and restored trim match what buyers have paid for in recent comps. When the wood is too damaged or the comps favor a cleaner modern look, we will show you that option instead. The finish plans in your estimate lay out both so you can decide, with the cost of each approach written out.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay anything before work begins?
faqs.a: No. Genstone requires no upfront payment. Each draw is matched to a finished stage of the Milwaukee job, and the final payment waits for completion and your sign-off. Dumpster and debris costs are included in the estimate, so cleanup on an old Milwaukee house with a full basement does not show up later as a surprise. Your field manager documents each completed stage before a draw is requested.

brrrr.title: BRRRR Rehab Contractor in Milwaukee, WI | Genstone
brrrr.metaDescription: BRRRR renovations in Milwaukee scoped for the refinance appraisal and for long-term rental durability in duplexes, bungalows and south side cottages.
brrrr.intro: Milwaukee is one of the Midwest's more practical places to run the BRRRR method, because purchase prices in many older neighborhoods still leave room for a meaningful rehab, and duplexes give you two rents from one roof. The trick is renovating to the right standard: enough to earn a strong appraisal when you refinance, durable enough to survive years of tenant turnover, and not so lavish that the money never comes back out. Genstone Construction plans BRRRR projects around that balance. We start with a free Pre-Offer Rehab Review that estimates repairs and refines the after-repair value, then write a scope that shows the appraiser a fully updated property and shows you a rental that will not need major work again soon. Genstone Financial also offers DSCR rental loans if you want to line up the refinance within the same group.

sections.h2: Renovating for the Milwaukee refinance appraisal
sections.body: Appraisers in Milwaukee lean on recent sales of similar homes nearby, and in neighborhoods like Jackson Park, Layton Park and the far northwest, those comps usually include houses with updated kitchens, newer mechanicals and finished hardwood. Your rehab has to look clearly in that class. The items that tend to move a refinance appraisal here are a functional modern kitchen, an updated bathroom, a newer furnace or boiler, an electrical service that will not raise lender questions, and a basement that is dry and clean. Cosmetic extras that do not show up in comps rarely earn their cost back. We document every system replacement with permits through the Department of Neighborhood Services and progress photos from your field manager, which gives you a clean package to hand the appraiser and the refinance lender. On a duplex, the appraiser will usually also consider rental income, so two finished, leasable units with separate entries and safe egress count for more than a showpiece kitchen in only one of them. Before you buy, our Pre-Offer Rehab Review checks whether the after-repair value you are counting on is supported by what has actually sold nearby.

sections.h2: Rental-grade choices that last in old Milwaukee houses
sections.body: Durability decisions in this city have a lot to do with water and cold. Luxury vinyl plank holds up better than carpet in duplex units and does not care about a damp lower level, but in rooms with good original oak, refinishing often costs less and appraises better. Plumbing is where shortcuts hurt most: replacing galvanized supply lines and failing cast-iron drains during the rehab prevents the midwinter leak calls that wreck a rental's numbers. Lead-safe window work and sealed, painted surfaces lower risk for families with young children, who are a large part of the tenant base. Exterior choices matter as well. Gutters, downspout extensions and regraded soil keep spring meltwater away from stone foundations, which keeps basements usable and reduces mold complaints. Heating deserves a hard look too. An old boiler that limps through the rehab will fail during a January cold snap, and replacing it then costs more and risks frozen pipes in an occupied unit. Building these choices into the first scope is what lets the property run for years after the refinance without a second round of capital.

The upper-and-lower duplex is the workhorse of Milwaukee BRRRR portfolios, and it brings its own scope questions. Many still run both units on one heating system or one electrical service, which complicates tenant billing and sometimes the refinance. Separating heat and power is often worth pricing, even if you decide to phase it. Shared basements need clean, secure laundry and storage areas so both households can use them. Rear stairs and two-story porches must meet code for guards and stability, since they are often the second exit for the upper unit. Polish flats on the south side raise a different question: whether the lower unit is truly rentable. Our Pre-Offer Rehab Review prices both units separately so you can see whether the second rent justifies the work before you buy. If you plan to refinance on income, it also helps to have both units finished and leased before the appraisal, which may mean sequencing the upper unit first so it can be rented while the lower one is completed.

faqs.q: What scope usually supports a Milwaukee BRRRR refinance?
faqs.a: In most older Milwaukee neighborhoods, the essentials are updated kitchen and bath, current mechanical systems, safe electrical without knob-and-tube, a dry basement, and fresh flooring and paint throughout. Beyond that, extras should be judged against local comparable sales. Our estimate can show a rental-grade plan and a stronger finish plan side by side so you can see what each does to your after-repair value.

faqs.q: Can the refinance stay within the Genstone Companies?
faqs.a: Yes. Our sister lender, Genstone Financial, writes DSCR rental loans for Milwaukee rentals, and it also handles flip loans, credit lines and new construction. Many investors use our renovation documentation, including scope, permits and progress photos, as part of their refinance package. You are free to use any lender you choose, and we will provide the same documentation package either way, at no extra charge.

faqs.q: How do draws work on a BRRRR project?
faqs.a: You pay nothing upfront. Your estimate includes a draw schedule tied to completed stages of work, and your field manager documents each stage with photos and notes before a draw is requested. The closing payment is made only once the work is finished and you sign off. Lenders funding the rehab generally appreciate that structure because it matches how they release construction funds and gives them a photo record of each stage.

rental-renovation.title: Rental Property Renovation in Milwaukee, WI | Genstone
rental-renovation.metaDescription: Single-family and duplex rental renovations in Milwaukee built for tenant turnover, lead-safe standards and cold winters. Portfolio-ready scopes and draws.
rental-renovation.intro: Rental owners in Milwaukee manage some of the oldest housing in the Midwest, and the cost of owning it comes down to how many emergency calls a property generates. A frozen pipe in a north side bungalow in January, a basement that floods every April, or a lead hazard flagged by an inspector can wipe out a year of profit. Genstone Construction renovates Milwaukee single-family and duplex rentals to a consistent portfolio standard aimed at fewer calls and faster turns. Our estimators build a detailed scope with labor, materials and a draw schedule, our field managers coordinate vetted local contractors, and the documentation stays visible to you and your property manager. For investors who want help after the rehab, Genstone Property Management and Genstone Field Services are part of the same group.

sections.h2: A durable rental standard for Milwaukee's older homes
sections.body: Owners with several Milwaukee rentals do better when every unit is built to the same specification. That usually means one or two flooring products that handle water and pets, a single paint color family that touches up easily, standard fixtures your maintenance team stocks, and kitchen cabinets and counters chosen for durability over trend. In older houses on the north and south sides, the standard also has to cover systems: replaced galvanized supply lines, a heating system that will handle cold snaps, safe electrical, working smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, and lead-safe surfaces. We write those standards into your scope so a house in Harambee and a house in Lincoln Village are finished the same way, which simplifies repairs and turns across the whole portfolio. A consistent spec also makes budgeting more predictable: once our estimators know your standard, each new acquisition can be scoped against it quickly, and your property manager knows exactly which paint, flooring and fixtures to order when something needs replacing. For institutional owners, that same spec can be tied to inspection checklists so every completed unit is verified before it is released for leasing.

sections.h2: Keeping Milwaukee rentals warm, dry and safe
sections.body: The rental problems that cost Milwaukee owners the most come from the climate and the basement. Ice dams on uninsulated attics push water into ceilings, so attic insulation and air sealing are often worth adding during the rehab. Spring snowmelt finds every crack in fieldstone walls, so gutters, downspout extensions, grading and, where needed, interior drain tile and a sump keep the lower level usable. Older boilers and furnaces fail at the worst time of year, and a replacement scheduled during the renovation is far cheaper than an emergency replacement with a tenant in place. Lead deserves its own attention because a large share of local renters are families. Lead-safe window and porch work during the renovation protects tenants and reduces the risk of a later order from city inspectors. Our scopes list these items separately so you can see what is protecting the asset and what is simply cosmetic.

Not every rental needs a full rehab. Between tenants, many Milwaukee owners need a fast turn: paint, flooring repairs, appliance checks, a deep clean and repair of whatever the last tenant broke. Genstone Field Services handles turn and make-ready work, along with inspections, occupied maintenance and code compliance work, so the same group that renovated the house can keep it ready. When a vacancy reveals a bigger problem, like a cracked cast-iron stack or a failing porch, the field manager can price it as a scoped project with its own draw schedule. Keep in mind our one-year workmanship warranty covers the work we perform, not tenant damage or normal wear, which is another reason a durable spec pays off over time. Turn timing in Milwaukee also follows the weather. Units that come vacant in winter are good candidates for interior work, while porch, roof and masonry items found during a winter turn are often logged and scheduled for spring. Your field manager keeps that list visible so deferred items do not get lost between tenants.

faqs.q: Do you renovate occupied Milwaukee rentals?
faqs.a: Often, yes, depending on the work involved. Many systems projects, such as heating replacement, electrical updates and exterior work, can be done with tenants in place if the schedule and access are planned carefully. Larger interior work is usually easier during a vacancy. Your field manager coordinates access windows with you or your property manager and keeps work areas safe for occupants.

faqs.q: Can you renovate several Milwaukee rentals at once?
faqs.a: Yes. Genstone works with individual investors, funds and institutional owners, and our network of licensed local contractors lets us run multiple properties in the same market. Each property gets its own scope, estimate and draw schedule, while the shared specification keeps finishes and fixtures consistent across the portfolio. Progress for every property is visible in one place, so you do not have to chase updates house by house.

faqs.q: What does the warranty cover on a rental renovation?
faqs.a: You get a one-year workmanship warranty on everything Genstone's crews install. What it leaves out is damage done by tenants and the normal wear any occupied home sees. If something we installed fails because of how it was installed, contact us and we will address it. Choosing durable, rental-grade materials up front reduces the wear-related repairs that fall outside any warranty, especially in high-turnover units near the university and downtown.

multifamily-renovation.title: Duplex & 2–4 Unit Renovation in Milwaukee, WI | Genstone
multifamily-renovation.metaDescription: Renovations for Milwaukee upper-and-lower duplexes, Polish flats and small 2–4 unit buildings, including phased work in occupied units and shared systems.
multifamily-renovation.h1: Duplex and 2–4 Unit Renovations in Milwaukee
multifamily-renovation.intro: Few cities have as many two-unit buildings as Milwaukee. The upper-and-lower duplex, with a front door for each unit and a shared basement below, fills entire blocks in Sherman Park, Riverwest, Washington Heights and the south side, and Polish flats add a second apartment under a raised cottage. These buildings can be strong investments, but their age and shared systems make renovations harder to plan than a single-family rehab. Genstone Construction renovates Milwaukee duplexes, triplexes and fourplexes for investors, phasing work around tenants when units are occupied and pricing shared systems separately so you understand the full cost. Every project begins with a free Pre-Offer Rehab Review and a detailed scope, and a single field manager runs the job from start to finish.

sections.body: The classic Milwaukee duplex places one apartment above another, each with its own front door, often with a rear stair that serves the upper unit. Built mostly from the 1900s through the 1920s, they share a basement, a roof and frequently a single heating plant. A typical renovation updates two kitchens and two bathrooms, but the more important work tends to be in the stairwells and the basement: safe rear stairs and porches, upgraded electrical, and plumbing stacks that serve both floors. Polish flats are different. The lower unit sits partly below grade because the cottage was lifted to add it, so ceiling height, window size, egress and moisture all limit what that unit can be. We look at both units separately during the Pre-Offer Rehab Review so you know whether the building is really two good rentals or one good rental and a costly lower level. Where a lower unit cannot reasonably meet egress and ceiling requirements, converting it to storage or returning the building to single-family use may be the more honest plan.

In many older Milwaukee two-unit buildings, the owner pays for heat for both units because one boiler serves the whole building. Separating heat into individual furnaces, and separating electrical services so each tenant pays their own bill, can improve net income and make the building easier to manage. It also adds work: new gas lines, new flue arrangements, more panels and, in some cases, utility coordination. We price separation as its own line so you can decide whether it pays off in your hold period. Shared water heaters, laundry and common stairways all need clear ownership in the plan as well. Work on these systems is permitted through the Department of Neighborhood Services and performed by licensed trades, with inspections built into the schedule. Fire separation between units is another shared-system item that older duplexes often lack. When ceilings or stairwells are opened, adding proper separation and hardwired, interconnected smoke alarms in each unit is usually the right call. Roofs and gutters serve both units too, so they are scheduled once for the building, ideally during warmer months, rather than split across two unit renovations.

Buying a duplex with one unit occupied is common in Milwaukee, and it changes the plan. We typically renovate the vacant unit fully first, then schedule shared-system work, such as heating, electrical service, roofing and the basement, with planned shutoffs and advance notice. When the second unit turns over, it gets its own interior renovation. This approach keeps rent coming in while the building is improved and avoids displacing a tenant mid-winter. Lead-safe practices are especially important in occupied buildings, since dust from the vacant unit can travel through shared stairs and basements. Your field manager posts updates so you and your property manager know what is happening on each floor. Timing matters with occupied buildings in this climate. Heating changeovers are best handled before the cold season, and any shutoff of water or power is scheduled for daytime hours with notice. When the work needs a basement, porch or stairwell that the tenant also uses, we plan a safe path and keep it clean at the end of each workday. A building that stays livable during renovation is far more likely to keep its existing tenant, which protects your income through the project.

faqs.q: Is it worth separating utilities in a Milwaukee duplex?
faqs.a: Often, but not always. Separate heat and electric shift ongoing costs to tenants and can make the building easier to refinance and sell, but the conversion has real costs for new equipment, gas piping and electrical work. Our estimate shows the separation as a distinct line so you can compare it to your expected hold period and rents before deciding.

faqs.q: Can you renovate a duplex while one unit is occupied?
faqs.a: Yes. Most occupied-building projects in Milwaukee start with a full renovation of the vacant unit, followed by scheduled work on shared systems and exteriors with notice to the tenant. The occupied unit is renovated when it turns over. Your field manager plans access, shutoffs and lead-safe containment around the people living there, including the shared basement, laundry and rear stairs.

faqs.q: Do you work on triplexes and fourplexes too?
faqs.a: Yes. Genstone renovates small multifamily properties from two to four units. Milwaukee has fewer fourplexes than duplexes, but they appear in older neighborhoods near the core and along commercial corridors. The same approach applies: a free Pre-Offer Rehab Review, a detailed scope that separates units and shared systems, and draws tied to completed work. Larger buildings usually add common-area lighting and more involved fire separation to the plan.

fha-203k.title: FHA 203(k) Contractor in Milwaukee, WI | Genstone
fha-203k.metaDescription: FHA 203(k) certified contractor for Milwaukee homebuyers, agents and lenders. Bids, consultant coordination and draws for bungalows, duplexes and cottages.
fha-203k.intro: The FHA 203(k) loan fits Milwaukee unusually well. The city has a deep supply of older bungalows, cottages and two-unit buildings that a buyer can afford but that will not pass a standard FHA appraisal without repairs, and the 203(k) program lets the buyer finance the purchase and the renovation in one mortgage. It can even be used on a duplex when the buyer lives in one unit. Genstone Construction is an FHA 203(k) Certified Contractor, and we work with Milwaukee buyers, real estate agents and loan officers to produce the bids, scope documents and draw schedules the program requires. Our goal is to keep the renovation side from delaying the closing and to deliver the finished work the loan paid for.

sections.h2: Standard or Limited 203(k) for Milwaukee houses
sections.body: Genstone's FHA 203(k) work uses the program thresholds as they are stated on our site: the minimum repair amount is $5,000, a 203(k) consultant inspection comes into play above $15,000, and the Limited 203(k) caps repairs at $75,000 and excludes structural work. In Milwaukee, a Limited 203(k) often fits a brick bungalow in Washington Heights or a post-war Cape Cod on the south side that needs a new furnace, updated electrical, new windows and a refreshed kitchen. A Standard 203(k) is the better tool when the scope reaches the foundation or structure, which is common on fieldstone basements, sagging porches or a duplex that needs both units rebuilt. Your loan officer makes the final call on program type, and our scope helps them make it accurately. The risk on older Milwaukee houses is that a project priced as Limited turns structural once walls or floors are opened, for example when a sagging beam under a bungalow or a failed porch footing shows up. Our estimators look for those signs early, so the buyer and lender choose the right program the first time rather than restructuring the loan midway through the process.

sections.h2: What Milwaukee 203(k) projects tend to include
sections.body: Many Milwaukee 203(k) purchases share a pattern. The house is older, often from before the 1930s, and the appraiser or consultant calls out health and safety items that must be corrected: peeling paint on a pre-1978 house, missing handrails on a front porch, a boiler or furnace near the end of its life, outdated or unsafe wiring, a leaking roof or a wet basement. Lead-safe work practices are required when painted surfaces are disturbed, and we plan them into the bid. Buyers often add improvements they want, such as a kitchen update or refinished floors, as long as the loan supports them. Two-unit buildings bring extra items like rear-stair repairs and separate smoke and carbon monoxide protection for each unit. We price required items and optional ones separately so the buyer and lender can see the difference clearly. That separation also helps if the appraisal comes in tight and the buyer has to trim the wish list without touching the items FHA requires.

sections.h2: Milwaukee 203(k) paperwork, consultants and draw inspections
sections.body: On a Standard 203(k), a HUD consultant prepares the work write-up, and our bid needs to match it line for line. We work from the consultant's report, flag items that will likely cost more once walls are open in an older Milwaukee house, and keep the paperwork consistent so the lender is not waiting on revisions. Once the loan closes, the lender holds the renovation money and pays it out in stages as each portion of work passes inspection. Your Genstone field manager coordinates those inspections, pulls permits from the Department of Neighborhood Services where needed, and documents each stage. Agents appreciate that structure because it keeps closings on track; buyers appreciate a single point of contact who knows the house. Many Milwaukee 203(k) buyers are first-time owners moving into an older home, so we explain what will happen at each stage, when they can expect access to the house, and how the remaining work will be sequenced if they move in before the final items are done. Seasonal timing matters here as well. A closing in late fall may mean exterior items such as porch or masonry repair are scheduled for spring, and we coordinate that plan with the lender so the draw schedule reflects it.

faqs.q: Can I use a 203(k) loan on a Milwaukee duplex?
faqs.a: FHA allows 203(k) financing on one- to four-unit properties when the borrower occupies one of the units as a primary residence. That makes the program a practical fit for Milwaukee's upper-and-lower duplexes. Your loan officer will confirm eligibility for the specific building, and we can prepare a bid that covers both units and any shared systems, such as heating, the roof and the basement.

faqs.q: How does a Milwaukee buyer get a 203(k) bid from Genstone?
faqs.a: Contact us with the property address, the listing details and, if available, the consultant's work write-up or inspection report. Our estimators review the house and prepare a scope and bid in the format your lender needs. If the consultant has not visited yet, we can start with a preliminary estimate to help the buyer and agent judge whether the deal works.

faqs.q: Are 203(k) draws paid upfront?
faqs.a: No. Renovation funds in a 203(k) loan are held and released in stages after completed work is inspected, which matches how Genstone works on every project. There is no upfront payment from the buyer to Genstone, and final payment follows completion and approval. Your field manager coordinates each draw inspection and provides the photos and documentation the lender requests, which keeps funds moving and the project on schedule.

reo-renovation.title: REO Property Renovation in Milwaukee, WI | Genstone
reo-renovation.metaDescription: REO and bank-owned renovations in Milwaukee for servicers, banks, GSEs and investors: freeze damage, code orders, vacant building rules and lead hazards.
reo-renovation.h1: REO and Bank-Owned Renovations in Milwaukee
reo-renovation.intro: Bank-owned and vacant houses in Milwaukee usually tell the same story when you open the door: the heat went off, the pipes froze, water ran into the basement, and the house sat long enough for mold, vandalism or a stack of city code orders. Repairing that kind of property takes a contractor who can secure it, document it, price it accurately and bring it back to marketable condition without guesswork. Genstone Construction works with mortgage servicers, banks, REITs, investment funds and investors buying REO, and we are a preferred contractor for Government-Sponsored Enterprises. Combined with Genstone Field Services for preservation, inspections and code compliance, we can manage a Milwaukee REO from initial securing through final repairs and listing.

sections.h2: Freeze damage and water in vacant Milwaukee houses
sections.body: A vacant house that loses heat in a Milwaukee winter rarely suffers just one burst pipe. Galvanized and copper supply lines split in exterior walls, boilers crack, toilet bowls and traps break, and the water that escapes runs down to the basement, where it soaks plaster, insulation and wood. When the thaw comes, mold follows. We start by assessing the full extent: pressure-testing the plumbing, checking the heating plant, and documenting water and mold damage with photos for the asset manager. Our scope separates emergency items, such as winterization, mold remediation and securing the structure, from the repairs needed to make the house marketable. That lets servicers and investors approve the urgent work quickly while weighing larger decisions with full information. Timing is critical. A Milwaukee house discovered without heat in December can keep deteriorating every day it sits, so winterization, draining lines, and securing doors and windows come first. Where a boiler system has frozen, radiators and piping need to be checked section by section before anyone decides whether to repair the system or replace it with forced air. The photo record we provide supports insurance claims and investor reporting as well as the repair decision.

sections.h2: Code orders and vacant building registration
sections.body: In Milwaukee, the Department of Neighborhood Services operates a vacant building registration program and issues code orders for conditions it finds on inspection, which can include broken windows, open doors, unsafe porches, overgrown lots and peeling paint. Orders follow the property, so a buyer of a bank-owned or tax-foreclosed house may inherit them. Our field team reviews outstanding orders as part of the scope and prices the work needed to clear each one. We handle permits for the repairs, coordinate reinspection and document compliance for the servicer or owner. Genstone Field Services can also take on ongoing preservation, such as lawn care, snow removal, lock changes and inspections, so a vacant property stays secure and in compliance while decisions are made. On the north side in particular, boarded windows and unsecured garages attract break-ins and scrapping of copper pipe and wiring, so routine inspections and quick resecuring help limit the damage a servicer later has to repair.

sections.h2: Bringing Milwaukee REO back to market
sections.body: Once a property is stabilized, the question becomes what level of repair supports the best outcome. Some REO in Milwaukee only needs to reach a condition that an FHA or conventional appraiser will accept, which typically means working heat, safe electrical, sound plumbing, a functioning kitchen and bath, and lead-safe surfaces. Others justify a fuller renovation because the neighborhood comps reward it. Our estimators prepare a scope that shows both paths, with detailed costs, so asset managers can choose with confidence. Throughout, documentation is ready for the client's review: photos, completed milestones, permits, lien waivers and inspections, with a field manager responsible from start to finish. Pricing decisions here are local. A bank-owned bungalow in Jackson Park may justify a buyer-ready kitchen and refinished floors because owner-occupants are bidding, while a duplex near Sherman Park may sell faster to investors at a stabilized, rent-ready standard. Our estimators look at the property and its street rather than applying one REO template across the city, and we keep the scope tied to what the property is most likely to sell for once repairs are done.

faqs.q: Who does Genstone work with on Milwaukee REO?
faqs.a: We work with mortgage servicers, banks managing bank-owned property, REITs, investment funds and individual investors buying REO, and we are a preferred contractor for Government-Sponsored Enterprises. Each client receives a detailed scope, documentation of work and a field manager who handles the property start to finish. Genstone Field Services adds preservation, inspections and code compliance for properties still in the pipeline.

faqs.q: Can you clear open code violations on a Milwaukee property?
faqs.a: Yes. We review existing orders from the Department of Neighborhood Services as part of the scope, price the repairs required to resolve them, pull any needed permits and coordinate reinspection. Genstone Field Services also handles code compliance work and ongoing preservation, which helps keep new violations from arising while the property sits vacant. Documentation of each resolved order is provided for your file.

faqs.q: What happens if a Milwaukee REO has mold?
faqs.a: Mold is common in vacant houses that froze or took on basement water. We document the affected areas, remove damaged materials, address the moisture source and include remediation as a defined line item in the scope. Correcting the water problem, whether a burst pipe, a leaking roof or poor drainage, is part of the plan so the mold does not return.
